standard.title: Health messages in community
standard.description: investigate a range of health messages and practices in their community and discuss their purposes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have identified health symbols, messages and strategies in their community that support their health and safety (AC9HPFP06).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate health messages and practices in their community and discuss their purposes.

nodes.label: Health symbols, labels and community messages
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify health symbols, medicine packaging and community health messages and understand the safety purposes they serve.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two health symbols or labels (e.g. poison labels, medicine packaging) and explain the safety action each communicates.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of health symbols, medicine labels, and community health messages; explain the safety purpose of each and what action it requires.
wider: Investigate how foods are marketed and promoted to children through advertisements in online spaces, supermarket placement and packaging, and discuss the health messages these convey
Compare health messages in different community contexts (school, supermarket, online) and identify whether they promote similar or different health behaviours
Explore how digital tools and screen-based products communicate health messages and discuss whether these are reliable
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that health symbols and messages communicate safety-relevant actions is prerequisite to investigating broader community health practices and purposes (Node 2). Without this anchor, students treat health messages as decorative rather than purposive.

response_modes.reason: Require students to decode the message: 'This symbol/label tells me __ because __'. The reasoning step prevents stopping at label identification without understanding the safety purpose.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two health symbols or labels
Explains the safety purpose or required action communicated by each

nodes.label: Food, health and community practices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss how eating a variety of fresh foods and community health practices influence health and wellbeing.
nodes.minimum_width: Using a reference such as the Australian Guide to Healthy Eating, describe how eating a variety of fresh foods can influence health and wellbeing.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how food choices and a range of community health practices influence health and wellbeing; discuss the purpose of these practices and why they matter.
wider: Explore sustainable practices students can implement in the classroom to improve health and wellbeing, such as composting food waste, creating an edible garden, or reducing single-use plastics
Investigate how foods are marketed to children and discuss how marketing influences food choice and health messages
Compare a food or health practice from a First Nations Australian or Asian Australian community with a familiar practice and discuss similarities and differences in health purpose

response_modes.reason: Community health practices vary widely — food, digital use, sustainability, medicine safety. Investigating across multiple practice types gives students a genuinely broader picture of what 'community health' encompasses.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Health practices across food, sustainability, digital wellbeing and cultural contexts provide qualitatively different examples of how communities promote health. Students who have only investigated food have a narrow conception of community health practices.
success_criteria: Describes how eating a variety of fresh foods can influence health and wellbeing
Identifies at least one community health practice and explains its purpose

nodes.label: Digital health rules and practices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create rules and apply them to implement healthy and manageable practices with their use of digital tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one rule for healthy digital tool use at school or home and explain its health purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Create and apply rules for healthy digital tool use; explain how these rules support health and wellbeing and discuss challenges to following them.
wider: Compare self-created digital use rules with recommendations from health organisations and evaluate whether the rules are consistent
Investigate how too much or unmanaged screen time can affect health and wellbeing, and propose specific rules to address the risks identified
Explore how digital rules at school might differ from those at home and discuss why context matters for health practice

response_modes.reason: This node connects health message literacy (Node 1) and community health practice understanding (Node 2) to the active health-practice demand of the descriptor. Tasks should require students to apply health knowledge to create and justify their own rules — not just identify what others recommend.

success_criteria: Describes at least one rule for healthy digital tool use
Explains how that rule supports health or wellbeing
